sources.title: Climate Risk Country Profile: Philippines
sources.organization: World Bank Group; Asian Development Bank
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed climatology through 2020; projections through 2080–2099; social vulnerability evidence includes earlier cited studies.
sources.methodology: World Bank–ADB country profile compiles climate datasets, referenced literature, observed climatology and CMIP5/KNMI projections.
sources.limitations: National synthesis; underlying social studies are dated. Global models cannot resolve many smaller islands, and precipitation projections are uncertain.

sources.title: DA, partners complete climate risk vulnerability assessment of BARMM provinces; recommend CRA options to guide investments, interventions
sources.organization: Philippines Department of Agriculture, Climate Resilient Agriculture Office
geographic_coverage: Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao
sources.temporal_coverage: Six-province CRVA completed in March 2024; projected crop suitability under RCP8.5, with projection period not stated on the webpage.
sources.methodology: DA CRAO's six-province CRVA used geospatial and secondary data validated by local offices.
sources.limitations: Only the official summary was inspected; underlying reports, datasets and projection horizons were unavailable.

sources.title: Understanding Climate, Conflict, and Environmental Impacts in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM): Workshop Report
sources.organization: Harvard Humanitarian Initiative; Mindanao State University–Iligan Institute of Technology
geographic_coverage: Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao
sources.temporal_coverage: Two-day workshop held 30–31 May 2023; case accounts describe historical and then-current conditions without consistent event dates.
sources.methodology: Two-day 2023 workshop; 70 actors invited, 29 organizations attended in person.
sources.limitations: Qualitative workshop accounts; local residents, Indigenous groups and other vulnerable people were absent; no causal testing.

sources.title: Philippines 2026 Joint Workplan: Summary Document
geographic_coverage: Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao
sources.temporal_coverage: Reports selected 2025 context and sets out 2026 activities under the 2024–2028 cooperation framework.
sources.methodology: UN 2026 workplan summarizes 2025 context, planned support and programme status.
sources.limitations: Self-reported or planned activity, not outcome evaluation or climate-conflict evidence.

sources.title: Philippines Country Climate and Development Report
sources.temporal_coverage: Official landing-page summary includes projection to 2040; report publication date not stated on the page.
sources.methodology: World Bank landing summary describes prior-work synthesis, partial-equilibrium sector analyses and CGE modeling.
sources.limitations: Landing page only; full report unavailable, so model assumptions and local estimates were not inspected.

claims.paraphrase: The 1991–2020 rainfall baseline varied from about 960 mm in southeast Mindanao to over 4,050 mm in central Luzon; periodic drought is linked to ENSO.
claims.limitations: Regional climatology is not a municipal vulnerability measure; ENSO linkage does not attribute individual droughts to anthropogenic climate change.

claims.paraphrase: Under RCP8.5, the profile projects about 3.4°C warming over Luzon and Mindanao in 2080–2099 using downscaled data; smaller-island and rainfall estimates remain uncertain.
claims.scenario: RCP8.5; downscaled KNMI Climate Explorer projection for 2080–2099
claims.limitations: This is a model projection, not an observed outcome; the source cautions that smaller islands and precipitation are poorly resolved.

claims.locator: Printed p. 23, Communities: Poverty, Inequality, and Disaster Vulnerability
claims.paraphrase: The profile says poorer farmers and communities are less able to afford water storage, irrigation and adaptation technology, while poorer groups are often more exposed to floods and mudflows.
claims.limitations: National synthesis based on cited studies, including older evidence; it does not identify specific municipalities.

claims.locator: Results of the vulnerability assessment, paragraphs on priority commodities and six provinces
claims.paraphrase: DA rates most priority-crop areas across the six BARMM provinces as highly climate-vulnerable.
institutions: Ministry of Fisheries, Agriculture and Agrarian Reform

claims.locator: Results of the vulnerability assessment, paragraph on hazard distribution
claims.paraphrase: Reported hazards vary: erosion/landslide across six provinces; flood in Lanao del Sur and Maguindanao provinces; surge in Basilan/Tawi-Tawi; drought in Sulu/Maguindanao del Norte.
claims.limitations: No probabilities or municipal-scale data are supplied.

claims.locator: Results of the vulnerability assessment, paragraphs on future crop suitability
claims.paraphrase: Under RCP8.5, rice/coconut conditions worsen in five provinces, banana in Lanao del Sur, and coconut in Basilan; rice suitability improves in Basilan.
claims.limitations: Model and crop-suitability thresholds are not supplied.

claims.locator: Results of the vulnerability assessment and Increasing climate resilience
claims.paraphrase: Municipalities across six provinces have generally low adaptive capacity from limited human, physical and economic capital; DA recommends crop diversification and nature-based options.
institutions: Ministry of Fisheries, Agriculture and Agrarian Reform
claims.limitations: Recommendations are proposed options, not evaluated outcomes.

claims.limitations: Workshop account, not a causal study.

claims.locator: Official report landing page, summary paragraphs on economic and household impacts
claims.paraphrase: The World Bank summary says that without action climate change could cut GDP by up to 13.6% by 2040, with poorest households most affected; effects vary within and across regions.
claims.scenario: The landing-page summary says 'if nothing is done' but does not specify a model scenario.
claims.limitations: Landing-page summary only; model assumptions, uncertainty range and named local estimates were not inspected.

search_audit.outcome: Found the HHI–MSU-IIT 2023 workshop report with qualitative, participant-attributed case mechanisms for Tandubas, Marawi, Sulu and Basilan; no empirical causal evaluation was located.

search_audit.outcome: The HHI workshop outline describes conflict diverting resources from adaptation and mitigation; the UN workplan documents BARMM service and governance constraints. No quantified reverse-pathway estimate was located.

search_audit.query: Philippines local climate adaptation resilience capacity BARMM provinces government NAP official report communities
search_audit.outcome: Found six-province CRVA capacity findings and recommendations, plus UN 2026 adaptation, WASH, displacement-protection and local-planning commitments. The NAP landing summary was accessible but the full PDF exceeded the tool limit.

gaps: The World Bank Philippines CCDR full report returned 403. One projected national finding is retained only from the clearly labeled official landing-page summary; assumptions and local estimates remain unverified.
The official National Adaptation Plan PDF exceeded the available fetch limit; no indexed passages were treated as evidence.
The underlying BARMM provincial CRVA reports were not inspected, so details beyond the DA webpage summary, including reference periods and municipal-level results, remain unavailable.

The strongest climate-conflict pathways are qualitative workshop case accounts from 2023, not representative or empirically tested causal estimates; the report says local residents, Indigenous communities and other vulnerable groups were not represented.
No recent quantitative study was located that estimates climate effects on violence or conflict effects on adaptation outcomes; this is an evidence-search gap, not evidence of no relationship.
